title: Review IP import on live site as a high-quality reader
description: No QA/review pass existed for the Integral Psychology import work (23 beads, all closed 2026-09-13) beyond the author's own verify_quotes.py + structural rowspan checks. Need an independent read-through on the actual published site (wilberwiki-preview-rufuspollock.flowershow.me, updated via fl . --yes) acting as a genuine reader, not the author: (1) Do the 11 charts/ pages actually render correctly and read as valuable, not just structurally valid HTML? (2) Do the new/extended concept and people pages read well and add real value, or does anything feel thin/padded? (3) Do cross-links (wikilinks) actually resolve? (4) Any broken images, obviously wrong table data, awkward prose, or navigation dead-ends a first-time visitor would hit? (5) Overall: is this genuinely publication-quality, and what's the single most important fix if not? Report findings, don't just say 'looks good' - the point is independent scrutiny of work that has, so far, only been self-reviewed.
notes: Independent subagent review (genuine-reader framing, not the author) found real issues: (1) dead link in concepts/integral-psychograph.md, (2) undefined BPM/Cs-uncs abbreviations, (3) a real transcription inconsistency on chart-4's Loevinger/Broughton table (silently dropped rows vs. the site-wide convention of showing blanks as '-'), (4) a stale 'once drafted' hedge, (5) a pre-existing stale note in habermas.md. All fixed, verified live on wilberwiki-preview post-republish (confirmed the dead link resolves correctly now, past a CDN-cache false alarm on first check). verify_quotes.py and the structural rowspan checker both still pass repo-wide. Commit 84780b9. Review found the work solid but not flawless - exactly the kind of scrutiny a self-review can't provide.
